nisab.title: Nisab Threshold
nisab.note: Nisab values are calculated using current market prices.

guideContent.definition: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam — an obligatory annual payment of 2.5% on qualifying wealth held above the nisab threshold for one lunar year.

nisab.gold: Nisab based on 85 grams of pure gold (scholarly consensus).
nisab.silver: Nisab based on 595 grams of pure silver. Many scholars prefer this as it benefits more people.
nisab.note: The silver nisab is typically lower in monetary value, meaning more Muslims are required to pay. Scholars differ on which to use; consult a local scholar.

rate.general: 2.5% (1/40) on cash, gold, silver, stocks, trade goods, and other investments
rate.agricultureRain: 10% (Ushr) on crops irrigated by rain or natural water

conditions: Muslim (Zakat is only obligatory on Muslims)
Owns wealth above the nisab threshold
Wealth held for one full lunar year (hawl) — agricultural produce is exempt from hawl
recipients: Those whose hearts are to be reconciled (new Muslims, etc.)
Those striving in the way of Allah (Fi Sabilillah)
zakatableAssets: Gold and silver (bullion, jewelry not in daily use)
Stocks and shares (calculate based on zakatable portion)
nonZakatableAssets: Tools and equipment used in work
Gold and silver jewelry worn daily (scholars differ on this)
guideContent.hawl: The hawl is the lunar year. Zakat becomes due once the nisab has been held for a complete lunar year (approximately 354 days). If wealth drops below nisab during the year and rises again, the year resets.
guideContent.disclaimer: This calculator provides an estimate based on common scholarly positions. For personal religious rulings, consult a qualified Islamic scholar (Mufti) in your region.
guideContent.source: Based on principles from the four major Sunni schools of law (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali).
